programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.sub-title: This Architect’s Own Home Shows What 'Less but Better' Really Means
programme.desc: Can a “less but better” approach create a richer home? In Separation Creek, along the Great Ocean Road in Victoria, MGAO designed a 90m² retreat for his family where restraint and the essentials are not limitations, but the source of its richness. Embodying the spirit of the local Australian beach shacks, a simple elevated rectangle frames the ocean. Rational planning and cost-conscious detailing recapture the relaxed, unfenced character of the township. Internally, a muted palette and veranda-like glazing blur the threshold between interior and nature. Here, simplicity reconnects the act of living with the coastal landscape, the community and history that surrounds it.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky
programme.desc: What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world? In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us. Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: The Ugly Truth of Fast Fashion & The Joy of Buying Less with Aja Barber
programme.desc: What if we all decided to buy less and buy better? In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast, we had the privilege of sitting down with fair-fashion campaigner, author, and thought-leader Aja Barber to learn about her own journey and career in the fashion and media industries, to touch on the real cost of fast fashion and overconsumption, and the joy that comes with buying less and buying better. In a world where we are taught to senselessly and unceasingly ‘BUY BUY BUY!’, overcoming overconsumption is as simple as: loving what we already have, fixing that which is broken, borrowing that which we only need for a short time, and seeking out secondhand as the first option when we want or need something new.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: Restore Nature & Bring Back Joy with Christabel Reed of Earthed
programme.desc: WE ALL NEED NATURE SKILLS. For millennia, knowledge and skillsets like tending land, saving seeds, maintaining soil health, and working within a community agricultural framework were passed down from generation to generation. In the midst of the industrial revolution, the creation of the 40-hour work week, and rapidly urbanising cities that don’t prioritise green spaces, these vital skills that connect us to the land are largely unknown to most in the West. In this episode of The Inspire Action Podcast, Ciara sits down with Christabel Reed, co-founder of platforms Advaya and Earthed. While Advaya centres around sharing knowledge and wisdom about mythology, ecology, and spirituality, Earthed offers free, online nature skills courses that aim to reconnect people with nature by getting them directly involved with it. Ciara and Christabel discuss ecological responsibility, bringing joy back to regeneration, land stewardship, barriers to entry, how our current systems can block our ability to be in nature as much as we need to be, and how everyone can work to restore our Earth.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.sub-title: Super Seaweed Solving the Plastic Problem (with Pierre Paslier, Notpla)
programme.desc: SUPER SEAWEED TO THE RESCUE! No, this seaweed hasn’t been genetically modified to fight off mutants–it’s just working to combat the plastic crisis, of course! One of the most dire issues our world today faces is the overproduction and overconsumption of plastic. With waste streams ill-equipped to handle the volume and varying types of plastic, as much as 23 million metric tonnes of plastic end up in our world’s waterways each year! Not only is this plastic choking marine life and ecosystems, but it’s also having devastating impacts on human health, communities, and economies. Founded in 2014, Notpla is on a mission to eliminate single-use plastic packaging with their innovative seaweed-based product. Their seaweed packaging is entirely biodegradable, organic, and made from seaweed harvested for industrial use (no fishy habitat destruction here!) In this episode, Ciara and Pierre discuss the plastic crisis, Notpla’s incredible 2022 Earthshot Prize win, how their work is eliminating tens of millions of pieces of single-use plastic across Europe and the UK, their future ambitions to use their product to better our world.

programme.title: Going Green: Green Green World
programme.sub-title: Every Building in 2050 Will Be Covered in MOSS!
programme.desc: This is why moss is the future of sustainable architecture! Alive Labs in London, are growing moss panels that can be installed in cities to help remove air pollution, suck up carbon dioxide, regulate the temperature and absorb rainwater! Moss’ potential has not been fully harnessed in architecture until now. It’s fire-resistant due to the modular shape, requires very little maintenance and the shapes can be customised to create moss artwork! The surrounding material is also the world's first bio receptive concrete made from fully organic materials. Building facades offer so much opportunity to reintroduce biodiversity into cities. This is a practical, easy to install solution, which we hope to see in cities around the world soon.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: Mistakes Can Happen At Any Time On Site
programme.desc: This video documents my first-ever cabinet installation for a paying client — from cutting melamine sheets in the workshop to scribing fillers on site and figuring things out the hard way. I walk through the entire cabinetry process: breaking down materials, sizing parts, installing drawer hardware, fixing mistakes, and dealing with walls that are nowhere near plumb. If you’re interested in cabinet making, furniture building, or starting a small woodworking business, this project shows what the job actually looks like — not just the clean highlight reel. This was the last project of 2025 for me, and a big learning curve — especially around quoting install time, managing client expectations, and understanding where profit actually comes from in cabinetry work. If you’re growing a trade business, thinking about taking on installs, or just curious how cabinet makers price jobs, this one’s for you.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: The Most Expensive Plywood I've Ever Worked With
programme.desc: I’m building a custom L-shaped shoe rack using premium Tasmanian Oak veneered plywood with a solid Victorian Ash seat. This project was a great client commission and a fun build, but with timber prices skyrocketing—and Victorian Ash becoming harder to source after the 2023 logging ban—it definitely pushed the limits of my margins. If you’re interested in furniture making, woodworking commissions, or want to see what it’s like working with high-end Tasmanian Oak plywood, this video walks through the full process: design, cutting, joinery, assembly, and installing the solid timber seat. I also talk about pricing custom furniture and how difficult Victorian Ash is becoming to find now that legislation has restricted harvesting.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: Is The Laser Industry Evolving Quick Enough?
programme.desc: The laser engraving world is exploding — but has it evolved too fast for beginners to keep up? In this video, I dive into my experience setting up the Omtech Turbo 756 60W CO₂ laser, from the initial unboxing to the unexpected issues that exposed some growing pains in the laser industry. If you’re new to laser engraving, thinking about buying a CO₂ laser, or just curious about how the industry is shifting from industrial to residential spaces, this is a must-watch. I cover what worked, what didn’t, and why it feels like the laser engraving community is still catching up to the speed of its own innovation. The laser engraving industry is growing fast — but are we ready for it? Let’s find out.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: The Most Beautiful Desk I've Ever Built
programme.desc: Ever thought about making a desk out of end grain? In this video, I take the idea of end grain parquet flooring and flip it on its head — turning it into a custom end grain desk build made entirely from timber offcuts. I walk through the full process of milling, gluing, pattern design, and flattening — essentially creating an end grain board on a massive scale. Along the way, I dive into the big question every woodworker faces: can you glue wood that moves to something that doesn’t? From concerns about wood movement, moisture, and cracking, to experimenting with epoxy and creative inlay work, this project became a long-term experiment in how far you can push the rules of woodworking. Watch the full video to see how I turned a pile of offcuts into a functional, geometric end grain desk — and find out if it actually survived.

His mother is still alive and living in Africa, Sebastian cuts short his trip to Paris and goes to Africa to look for his mother without his dad permission after discovering his mother is alive. He falls in trouble by loving a woman of a tough village son of a chief which is prohibited to fall in love for a woman with having performed Imbalu 'circumcision' cultural practiced which is a passage from being a boy to become a man every man who has never done Imbalu still remains a boy who's never given privilege of marrying and decision making. And went against the cultural values when he refused to be circumcised...

programme.title: Kiomi Kiumeni
programme.desc: An affluent guy goes to visit his girlfriend home in the ghetto where all kinds of drama ensues. Kiumeni is a Swahili comedy/love story that brings two distinct worlds together; when an affluent guy goes to visit his less privileged girlfriend at her home in the ghetto. Their young love is suddenly overcome with challenges, near-death experiences and hilarious comebacks that put their union to the test

programme.title: The Far Frontier
programme.desc: Willis Newcomb and Bart Carroll head a gang engaged in smuggling wanted-American criminals back into the United States from Mexico. Operating from Sharperville, an oil town on the American side of the border, they transport their human cargo in oil drums loaded on trucks. Border Patrolman Tom Sharper intercepts one of the trucks but is overpowered and left for dead. Carroll, having already been paid for the job and not wanting any evidence to walk around, get caught and lead back to him, backs the human-cargo trucks to the edge of a cliff and sends the drums crashing to the boulder far below. Judge Cookie Bullfincher and Border Patrolman Roy Rogers conduct a search for the missing Tom, but the crooks have gone back for him and find him in a state of amnesia. They rob the bank and pin it on Tom. It is now up to Roy to clear his friend and also put an end to Carroll's human-smuggling racket.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

Le site est proche des sources perennes de la riviere Yarkon et fait desormais partie du parc national de Yarkon en Israel. programme.title: Impostora
programme.desc: Nimfa, an ugly street vender, meets jeremy, a talented plastice surgeon, in a car accident. In her desire to change her life and escape her situation, she willingly undergoes complete facial reconstruction. She later discovers that her face is copied from Rosette, a wealthy and married woman who happens to be jeremy's lover. Rosette wants to escape her life with her husband and their kids. Forced to accept her circumstance, Nimfa becomes an imposer so Rosette and Jeremy can get away with their affair.

programme.desc: La basilique de Jesus l’Adolescent, egalement appelee simplement eglise salesienne, est une eglise catholique a Nazareth en Israel, appartenant aux Salesiens de Don Bosco. Situee a cote de l’ecole des Salesiens, elle a ete construite entre 1906 et 1923 sur une colline appelee Mont du Debut, qui surplombe la ville, où, selon la tradition, Jesus a passe sa jeunesse. De la terrasse de l’eglise, la vue sur la vieille ville de Nazareth est exceptionnelle, divisee en quartiers orthodoxe, catholique romain et musulman.

Filmmaker Erik Lemke asks 19 representatives of the homeopathic mainstream - most of whom have a medical education - the same questions, and skillfully intercuts their contradictory answers.

programme.title: El Gran Inventario del Planeta: Nueva Caledonia, tierra de maravillas terrestres
programme.desc: Con la tripulación de El Explorador, descubra los confines del hemisferio sur, rumbo al archipiélago Austral. El barco atraca en Rairoa, el puerto y pueblo principal de Raivavae. Una vez desembarcado el helicóptero, el equipo se pone en marcha para ofrecer imágenes aéreas del paraíso.

programme.title: Des Racines et des ailes - Passion Patrimoine
programme.sub-title: Sur les rives de la Garonne
programme.desc: Des Pyrenees espagnoles ou elle prend sa source, au vaste estuaire de la Gironde ou elle se jette, la Garonne parcourt plus de 600 kilometres a travers le Comminges, l'Agenais ou l'Entre-deux-Mers. Le fleuve evolue au cours de ce long voyage. L'apport de ses affluents, comme la Neste, l'Ariege, le Tarn et le Lot, modifie son visage. A bord d'un helicoptere, Didier Taillefer part en Espagne pour faire des photos aeriennes de l'une des principales sources du fleuve : le Trou du Toro. Ce site exceptionnel est situe au pied du massif de la Maladeta, ou la Garonne disparaît sous terre avant de reapparaître au Val d'Artan. Au coeur des Pyrenees, le fleuve donne naissance a un jardin de Cocagne : le Comminges. Dans le village de Huos, Remy Martin a amenage un verger-potager bio sur un ancien meandre.

programme.title: Who Am I Happy

programme.desc: La loca geografía de la tierra de los hombres. El archipiélago de las Marquesas, formado por catorce islotes, es el más septentrional de los archipiélagos de Polinesia y, sin duda, el más aislado del mundo.

The two men stay in the forest but can't find her. Initially, Malte Wirtz had wanted to shoot a romantic comedy in Cologne's Königsforst.

programme.title: El Gran Inventario del Planeta: Polinesia de Gambier
programme.desc: The Explorers presenta una imagen no sólo bella, sino profundamente viva. En estas balsas de coral abandonadas por los volcanes, la vida se ha reinventado. De la nada, poco a poco, ha creado oasis, cada vez más ricos, con su propio equilibrio y tempo, el latido de los canales que riegan el atolón.

programme.title: Black Panther – The Story of Emilie and Jacob
programme.desc: Emilie shares her sadness about the loss of their parents, but also a well-hidden secret. Can the two siblings really live a love that must remain invisible, a love that is source of hope and fear at the same time. Samuel Perriard's stylized corporeality - the extremely closeup, high resolution erotic sequences - are an ode to the beauty of the forbidden.

programme.title: Iditarod, la derniere course Nicolas Vanier
programme.desc: L’iditarod est la course de chiens de traineaux la plus emblematique au monde traversant tout l’Alaska sur 1700km. Nicolas Vanier, grand passionne des territoires du Grand Nord et musher experimente, est celebre pour ses defis polaires sur tous les territoires glaces. L’Iditarod sera son ultime pari.

programme.title: Tiempo Para Nuestro Cuerpo y Mente
programme.desc: Una serie dedicada al bienestar fisico y mental a traves de ejercicios, yoga, pilates y diferentes practicas saludables. Especialistas y entrenadores comparten clases, tecnicas y experiencias que inspiran a cuidar el cuerpo, encontrar equilibrio y vivir de forma mas consciente.

programme.title: Deliciosisimo

programme.title: Amor Musical
programme.desc: Todo inicia cuando son transferidos a la escuela Jung San que recibe auspicio por parte de una fundación millonaria y poderosa. Como es de esperarse, los días escolares en esta escuela se convierte en una lucha sin fin. Cada día enfrentan el gran abismo entre el rico y el pobre. Ante la cruda realidad, en lo único que pueden confiar es en su música. Tocar con sus amigos es la única cosa que los mantiene vivos, al mismo tiempo, Su música los hace brillar por encima de los demás. “Amor Musical” es un drama musical como nunca antes visto; al mejor estilo y creado para el sentimiento punk.

They get "help" from an older lady who shares stories that might be just a bit too intimate.

programme.title: Shot In The Dark
programme.desc: "I only understood how powerful light is after I went blind." A documentary about three blind photographers: Pete Eckert, Sonia Soberats and Bruce Hall - three exhibiting artists. What do they see in their mind's eyes? "Even with no input the brain keeps creating images," says Pete Eckert. Sonia Soberats states, "I only understood how powerful light is after I went blind.

Le parc comprend Tel Ashkelon et les vestiges de l’ancienne Ashkelon, entoures par la muraille cananeenne, ainsi que 1 000 dunams de dunes de sable et de kurkar au sud du parc, entre la muraille et le site du pipeline Eilat-Ashkelon.

Pero también para descubrir la cultura de los primeros habitantes de la isla, los melanesios.

programme.title: Impostora
programme.desc: Nimfa, an ugly street vender, meets jeremy, a talented plastice surgeon, in a car accident. To compensate for what happened, jeremy offers to help Nimfa by giving her new face through surgery. In her desire to change her life and escape her situation, she willingly undergoes complete facial reconstruction. She later discovers that her face is copied from Rosette, a wealthy and married woman who happens to be jeremy's lover. Rosette wants to escape her life with her husband and their kids. Forced to accept her circumstance, Nimfa becomes an imposer so Rosette and Jeremy can get away with their affair.

programme.desc: Lokasjonen for Roadrace-konkurransen er Arctic Circle Raceway! Det er første gangen Alf skal kjøre på vått føre, og Steffen har endelig fått orden på sykkelen sin. Men hos Team Kaos kan alt skje, og løpet tar en rask og uforventet vending.

programme.title: Min Motorsport - Siste løp i Superbike 2017!
programme.desc: Om serien: I denne serien følger vi forskjellige motorsportutøvere gjennom deres racingsesong. Sporten, målene og forutsetningene er forskjellige, men felles for dem alle er lidenskapen for sporten sin og miljøet de er i.

programme.title: Min Motorsport - Roadracing med Steffen og Team Kaos
programme.desc: Steffen er en del av vennegjengen Team Kaos, og de har virkelig fortjent navnet sitt. De kjører alle roadracing,og medlemmene har forskjellig erfaring og konkurrerer i ulike klasser. Vi møter dem på Vålerbanen for sesongens første testkjøring.

programme.title: Garasjen - Kim Jannike sin BMW, Grensetreffet i Halden og nytt eksosanlegg!
programme.desc: Kim Jannike har bygget seg en BMW, og denne skal brukes i drifting, men når hun skal prøvekjøre bilen med Asgeir går ikke alt som planlagt. Det er også tid for Grensetreffet i Halden, hvor det er mange flotte biler å se på.

programme.title: Garasjen - Spesiell drømmebil, Finnskogfestivalen og en låve full av amcar
programme.desc: I denne episoden av Garasjen er det klart for Finnskogfestivalen. Der møter vi Line Myrvold og Leif André Ødegaard som skal konkurrere i bilcross og rallycross. Torbjørn viser oss også hans noe spesielle drømmebil.

programme.title: Garasjen - Nyinnkjøpt Ferrari, Volvo 142 og finale på Finnskogfestivalen
programme.desc: Vi møter vi Ivar og Asgeir. De har kjøpt en Volvo 142, som de skal bygge om til en rask rallybil for å delta i Rallye Monte-Carlo Historique. I Drammen treffer vi Arild Olsen som har kjøpt en Ferrari han ikke har sett på nett.

programme.title: Garasjen - Mekking av både Ferrari og Volvo 142, og et lite lakk kurs
programme.desc: Halvor Sunde fra Risør åpner dørene til sin egen garasje, som blant annet huser en strøken Hotrod. Asgeir besøker Arild og hans Ferrari, og gir ham en hjelpende hånd når motoren skal settes inn. Videre går turen til Gatebil on ice i Sigdal.

programme.title: Jeg går elektrisk - Jeg går elektrisk...med Kia e-Soul
programme.desc: Ståle tester Kie e-Soul, som er proppfull av teknologi. Men kan det bli for mye av det gode?

programme.title: Jeg går elektrisk - Jeg går elektrisk...med Audi e-tron GT
programme.desc: Audi eTron har vært en stor salgsuksess i Norge, og nå har de kommet med en mer sportslig utgave: Audi eTron GT. Vil Ståle sette like stor pris på denne sportslige utgaven, som han satte på Porsche Taycans sportlige utgave?

programme.title: Jeg går elektrisk - Jeg går elektrisk...med Skoda Enyaq iV
programme.desc: Bilverden utvikler seg, og elbiler blir mer og mer vanlig. Med den skeptiske motorentusiasten Ståle Eskeland i spissen får vi et innblikk i hvordan bilene faktisk er å kjøre. Et biltest-program av elbiler, fra en motorelskers perspektiv.

programme.title: Jeg går elektrisk - Jeg går elektrisk...med BMW i3
programme.desc: Denne gangen tester Ståle BMW i3. Men kan den egentlig kalles for en sporty bil?

programme.title: Jeg går elektrisk - Jeg går elektrisk...med Nissan Leaf
programme.desc: Denne gangen tester Ståle hvordan Nissan Leaf er å kjøre. Fortjener virkelig Nissan Leaf "bestselger" tittelen sin? Vi får høre hva Ståle har å si.

programme.title: Milestones - Milestones 1990-2007
programme.desc: Mellom 1990 og 2007 utvides bilindustrien. Toyota blir verdensomspennende, og sportsbilene blir mer og mer modne. Bruktbilmarkedet blomstrer og det nye årtusenet bringer mange nyvinninger.

programme.title: Milestones - Milestones 1886-1930
programme.desc: Bilen har eksistert i over 100 år, og det har vært en lang vei å gå fra første testkjøring til ABS, Air condition og automatgir. Mer enn et århundre med utvikling, og vogna med motor blir stadig oppgradert til mer sofistikerte biler.

programme.title: Milestones - Milestones 1930-1940
programme.desc: Bilen har eksistert i over 100 år, og det har vært en lang vei å gå fra første testkjøring til ABS, Air condition og automatgir. Mer enn et århundre med utvikling, og vogna med motor blir stadig oppgradert til mer sofistikerte biler.

programme.title: Milestones - Milestones 1980-1990
programme.desc: 80-tallet er preget av racinglegender. En ny verdensmester kommer på banen, og viser frem motorer med 1.200 hester. Porche 959 er den raskeste landeveisbilen i verden. Motorsport har mer å si enn noen gang, og tiårene er fyllt med store motorer.

programme.title: Garasjen - Testkjøring av Volvo 142, Formula Offroad bygging og motivlakkering av Audi.
programme.desc: Ivar og Asgeir skal teste Volvoen de har mekket på, og får noen tips på kjøreteknikk av en som virkelig kan det. Norges beste varebilsjåfør skal kåres. Vi møter også Sigurjon som skal bygge seg en Formula offroad bil helt fra scratch.

programme.title: Garasjen - Drifting på Rudskogen, Lille Bjørn og Rally Monte Carlo Historiqe start!
programme.desc: Vi treffer Tor Anders Ringnes, som lenge har jobbet med å gjøre bilen klar for driftssesongen. Bilen skal være klar til Rudskogen motorfestival. Videre går turen til Jarle i Risør, som åpner dørene til garasjen sin.

programme.title: Garasjen - Rally Monte Carlo Historiqe, Garasjebesøk i Kristiansand og ferdigstilling av Audien!
programme.desc: Ivar og Asgeir deltar i Rallye Monte Carlo Historique. Vi besøker garasjen til Melvin i Kristiansand. Asgeir har jobbet hardt for å få ferdig Audien sin. Nå er det klart for siste finish, før bilen skal EU-godkjennes.

programme.title: Garasjen - Pål Anders Ullevålseter, NTCC i Århus og en ødelagt kluch.
programme.desc: Vi blir med Asgeir Borgemoen inn i garasjene til en rekke motorentusiaster rundt om i Norge. Kjøretøyene og prosjektene varierer, men lidenskapen for prosjektene sine er like stor hos dem alle. Det er utrolig hva som skjuler seg bak en garasjeport!

programme.title: Bloch spielt - Gran Turismo 7 mit VR-Brille: Sehr geil, aber der Magen rebelliert!
programme.desc: Gran Turismo funktioniert jetzt auch mit der Sony VR2-Brille! Da stürzt Alex sich gleich in die Renn-Action. Allerdings hat er die Rechnung ohne seinen Magen gemacht...

programme.title: Einzeltest
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto.

programme.title: Vorfahrt
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Nio Battery-Swap
programme.desc: Der chinesische Autohersteller Nio geht das Thema "E-Auto laden" anders an als die Konkurrenz. In sogenannten Battery-Swap-Stations soll der Akku innerhalb von nur fünf Minuten gewechselt werden. Ist das die Zukunft der Elektromobilität? Alexander Bloch testet die Anlage und klärt die 9 größten Irrtümer zum Akkuwechsel beim E-Auto.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Golf 7
programme.desc: Der VW Golf 7 ist eines der meistverkauften und beliebtesten Modelle des Volkswagenkonzerns. Worauf man beim Kauf eines gebrauchten Golf 7 achten muss erklärt Alexander Bloch. Egal ob Probleme mit dem AGR-Ventil, dem DSG-Getriebe und Rost, die Schwachstellen und guten Seiten des Wolfsburger Dauerbrenners kommen hier zum Vorschein.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - 1.000.000 Kilometer
programme.desc: In der 100. Folge von Bloch erklärt kümmert sich Alex um das Thema Dauerläufer: Wie hält dein Auto ewig? Im Mittelpunkt steht ein Lexus LS400 mit einer Million Kilometer auf der Uhr. Wie fährt sich so ein Kilometerfresser eigentlich? Und was muss man tun, damit das eigene Auto auch das Zeug zum Dauerläufer hat? Alex Bloch erklärt euch 10 wichtige Regeln - das wird gut!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - E-Autos 2023
programme.desc: Die Lieferzeiten bei Elektroautos sind lang. Doch zumindest wird 2023 die Auswahl deutlich größer. Besonders die chinesischen Hersteller wollen angreifen und zeigen zahlreiche Neuheiten. Aber auch die deutschen Produzenten legen nach. Alexander Bloch zeigt seine 10 Highlights für das Jahr 2023. Hier seht ihr seine Favoriten.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Sicherheits-Irrtümer
programme.desc: Welche Autos sind am sichersten? Welche Aussagekraft haben Crashtests überhaupt? Warum spielt die Farbe eines Autos in der Unfallstatistik eine Rolle? Die Antwort auf diese Fragen und weitere spannende Informationen rund um das Thema Verkehrssicherheit gibt es in dieser Folge Bloch erklärt. Zudem findet Alexander Bloch unter den Testdummies einen neuen Freund: Thor!

programme.title: Die 7
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Porsche Taycan im E-Auto-Supertest
programme.desc: Porsche hat den Taycan umfangreich überarbeitet und in vielen Disziplinen verbessert. Die Batterie wird größer und kann schneller Laden. Alex Bloch fährt den Basis Taycan mit großer Batterie im E-Auto-Supertest und kommt aus dem Grinsen nicht mehr raus. Wie die Chancen stehen, dass der Taycan auf die Pole Position der Elektroautos fährt, seht ihr im Video.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der MG4 Electric im E-Auto Supertest
programme.desc: Der MG4 schwimmt auf der Erfolgswelle! Der Überflieger befindet sich unter den Top 5 der meistverkauften Elektroautos in Deutschland. Was der chinesischen Kompaktstromer im Vergleich zum Opel Astra Electric und dem VW ID.3 drauf hat, klärt Alexander Bloch.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Opel Astra Electric im EAS
programme.desc: Kein anderes Auto hat Alexander Bloch bisher in ein solches Wechselbad der Gefühle geschmissen. Von „sensationell!“ bis „macht ihr Witze?“ ist alles dabei. Was die Stärken und Schwächen des Opel Astra Electric sind und ob er sich gegen den VW ID.3 behaupten kann, erfahrt ihr hier!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Mercedes E-Actros 600: Die 5 GIGA-Fakten zum neuen Elektro-Truck
programme.desc: Mercedes-Benz Trucks präsentiert den E-Actros 600, einen batterieelektrischen 40-Tonner, der ohne Zwischenladung mehr als 500 Kilometer weit fahren soll. Alexander Bloch durfte sich den Elektro-LKW bereits exklusiv anschauen und erklärt die 5 Giga-Fakten zum neuen Mercedes E-Actros 600.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Sparen mit dem Elektroauto: Das bringt was - und das bringt nichts!
programme.desc: Auch zum Elektroauto gibt es eine Vielzahl an Spartipps. Doch bringen die wirklich was? Alexander Bloch erklärt welche Tipps sinnvoll sind - und welche ihr euch sparen könnt.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Langstreckenstar Hyundai Ioniq 6: Fast wie ein Verbrenner!
programme.desc: Oft fließt die Reichenweitenangst in die Kaufentscheidung von Elektro-Autos ein. Bei Verbrennern stellt sich diese Frage gar nicht: die Reichweiten sind hoch und nach einem fünfminütigen Tankstopp geht es für gewöhnlich weiter. Eignen sich Elektro-Autos auch als Reisebegleiter? Wie viel Reichweite ist wirklich nötig? Und wie viel Zeit muss ich für das Laden einplanen? All das beantwortet Alexander Bloch anhand des Hyundai Ioniq 6.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Ist Drehmoment wichtiger als Leistung? Die 5 größten Irrtümer zu PS & Co.
programme.desc: PS, Kilowatt und Newtonmeter benutzt man häufig, wenn man über Autos spricht. Dabei gibt es hier einige Stolperfallen. Sind PS in allen Ländern gleich? Newtonmeter gibt es nur beim Drehmoment? Alexander Bloch erklärt die 5 größten Irrtümer zu PS, Kilowatt und Co.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Kein Motoröl im E-Auto? 4 Irrtümer zu Öl im Elektroauto
programme.desc: Ein E-Auto braucht kein Öl und schon gar kein Motoröl. Ist das wirklich so? Chief Explanation Officer Alexander Bloch ist ins Forschungs- und Entwicklungszentrum von Petronas Lubricants gefahren, um mit den größten Öl-Irrtümern rund um die Elektromobilität und die Zukunft von Schmier- und Motorölen aufzuräumen.

programme.title: Einzeltest
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - BMW i5: Deutschland kann es doch!
programme.desc: Alexander Bloch bittet den BMW i5 eDrive40 zu einem ersten Check. Im ersten rein elektrischen 5er BMW sorgt der gleiche Elektromotor wie im BMW i4 eDrive40 für Vortrieb. Nun hat die E-Maschine mit mehr Gewicht zu kämpfen. Wie sich das auf die Reichweite und den Verbrauch auswirkt, ermittelt Bloch vor laufender Kamera. Dank Hands-Free-Driving geht das auch ohne Hände am Steuer.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Autonomes Fahren - Blick in die Zukunft mit autoELF
programme.desc: Die autoELF entstand im Projekt UNICARagil - ein autonomes Fahrzeug gemäß Level 4. Um autonom fahren zu können, braucht es viele verschiedene Sensoren - und die sind teuer. Alex Bloch lässt sich mit verschiedenen Manövern über die Teststrecke chauffieren und bespricht im Interview mit Prof. Dr.-Ing. Steven Peters die autonome Zukunft.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Die 5 Todsünden auf den ersten 1.000 km
programme.desc: Man hat lange gewartet und endlich ist es soweit: der Neuwagen ist da! Am liebsten würde man jetzt sofort ordentlich Gas geben. Aber Moment mal, war da nicht irgendwas? So ein neues Auto muss doch erst eingefahren werden, oder? Alexander Bloch erklärt, was auf den ersten 1.000 Kilometern zu beachten ist: Motor, Turbo, Bremsen, Dämpfer, Reifen - es gibt eine Menge zu tun.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - E-Auto-Highlights 2024: Auch ohne Förderung ein gutes Jahr
programme.desc: Auch 2024 kürt Alex Bloch wieder seine E-Auto-Highlights. Hier seht ihr die Top-Neuheiten: Günstig, schnell, viel Platz oder Offroad-tauglich. Hier ist für jeden etwas dabei!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Straße weiß, Akku leer? 4 E-Auto Winter-Mythen
programme.desc: Wenn es draußen frostig und kalt ist, kommt man mit dem E-Auto nur noch halb soweit und auch das Aufladen dauert doppelt so lang. Ist das wirklich so? Eisbär Alexander Bloch räumt mit den 4 gängigsten Winter-Mythen zu E-Autos auf.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Renault R5 im E-Auto-Supertest
programme.desc: Der Renault 5 feiert sein Comeback: Als elektrischer Kleinwagen im Retro-Design. Doch Optik ist nicht alles. Alexander Bloch prüft im E-Auto-Supertest, was der neue R5 bei Technik, Komfort und Platzangebot drauf hat. Auch Verbrauch, Reichweite und Dynamik stehen im Fokus. Ist der Renault 5 zurecht zum Auto des Jahres 2025 gewählt worden?

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der VW ID.7 im E-Auto-Supertest
programme.desc: Der ID.7 stellt die vierte Stufe der Elektromobilität bei VW dar. Die Fünf-Meter-Limo kommt mit einem neuen Elektromotor, neuen Features und Software und einer verbesserten Aerodynamik daher. Ob der ID.7 das beste Elektroauto unter 100.000 Euro im Supertest werden kann und damit den BWW i4 eDrive 40 entthront, prüft Alex im E-Auto Supertest.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Ford Explorer im Supertest – Wie gut ist er wirklich?
programme.desc: Der neue Ford Explorer mit 77 kWh Akku und Heckantrieb steht im Elektroauto-Supertest! Wie schlägt er sich in Effizienz, Qualität, Dynamik und Komfort? Ist er eine echte Alternative zu VW? Alex Bloch nimmt ihn genau unter die Lupe. Jetzt anschauen!

Wie die Chancen stehen, dass der Taycan auf die Pole Position der Elektroautos fährt, seht ihr im Video.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der MG4 Electric im E-Auto Supertest

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Opel Astra Electric im EAS
programme.desc: Kein anderes Auto hat Alexander Bloch bisher in ein solches Wechselbad der Gefühle geschmissen. Von „sensationell!“ bis „macht ihr Witze?“ ist alles dabei. Was die Stärken und Schwächen des Opel Astra Electric sind und ob er sich gegen den VW ID.3 behaupten kann, erfahrt ihr hier!

programme.title: 2012: Supernova

programme.title: Age Of Dinosaurs

programme.title: Headline：A Chinese village run by a CEO
programme.desc: In a Dai village called "Manluanzhan" near China's southwestern border, a full-time rural CEO manages the books and coordinates business operations at homestays, cafés, breweries, and other shops. But how to benefit from rural tourism without losing the village charm? In Manluanzhan, a fresh experiment is unfolding – one where villagers remain participants, investors, and decision-makers, but a CEO enters the fray to help defend their interests.

programme.title: Meet China: Flying into the Future, Growing a Greener City, and Connecting Business to the World
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how the future is taking shape across different corners of China and beyond. From Guangzhou's rising low-altitude economy powered by electric flying cars, to Xiamen's practical path toward zero-carbon urban life, we see how innovation is changing the way people live and cities grow. We also step into China's booming livestream shopping culture, where commerce becomes community, and travel to Malaysia's rice fields, where Chinese agricultural expertise is helping improve harvests and food security. This episode reveals how technology, industry and creativity are turning bold ideas into everyday reality.

programme.title: Live: Beyond the buzz: What do young Americans really think about China-US relations?
programme.desc: What happens when young Americans experience China beyond the headlines? Join CGTN for a candid conversation with US creators and students living in China as they share firsthand perspectives on daily life, consumer trends, innovation, and how these experiences are reshaping their understanding of China's economic dynamism and China-US connections.

programme.title: China's Industrial Chains: Threads of Resilience
programme.desc: What is clothing made from? Not just cotton or wool. Sometimes, it starts with a single drop of oil! Follow CGTN as we reveal how a drop of crude oil transforms into our clothes, uncovering a complex and fascinating journey of the textile and garment manufacturing process. Follow CGTN's Wang Tianyu and take a closer look at China's textile and garment industry, and unravel the threads that connect China's industrial past, present and future.

programme.title: Meet China: Flying into the Future, Growing a Greener City, and Connecting Business to the World
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how the future is taking shape across different corners of China and beyond. From Guangzhou's rising low-altitude economy powered by electric flying cars, to Xiamen's practical path toward zero-carbon urban life, we see how innovation is changing the way people live and cities grow. We also step into China's booming livestream shopping culture, where commerce becomes community, and travel to Malaysia's rice fields, where Chinese agricultural expertise is helping improve harvests and food security. This episode reveals how technology, industry and creativity are turning bold ideas into everyday reality.

programme.title: Live: Beyond the buzz: What do young Americans really think about China-US relations?
programme.desc: What happens when young Americans experience China beyond the headlines? Join CGTN for a candid conversation with US creators and students living in China as they share firsthand perspectives on daily life, consumer trends, innovation, and how these experiences are reshaping their understanding of China's economic dynamism and China-US connections.

programme.title: China's Industrial Chains: Threads of Resilience
programme.desc: What is clothing made from? Not just cotton or wool. Sometimes, it starts with a single drop of oil! Follow CGTN as we reveal how a drop of crude oil transforms into our clothes, uncovering a complex and fascinating journey of the textile and garment manufacturing process. Follow CGTN's Wang Tianyu and take a closer look at China's textile and garment industry, and unravel the threads that connect China's industrial past, present and future.

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: Rhythms of the Forest: A Sound of Li Instruments
programme.desc: Li bamboo and wood instruments offer a journey into the unique sounds of Hainan's Li ethnic group. Explore the ancient craftsmanship and musical heritage, from the resonant tones of bamboo flutes to the percussive rhythms of wooden drums. Experience the natural melodies that tell the stories of the Li people.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Silversmith
programme.desc: In this episode, Eva May steps into Maliao Village — a century-old silversmith village nestled in Leishan, Guizhou Province. Over the course of a week, she dives into the craft and daily lives of Miao men who carry on the silversmithing legacy. She works side by side with local silversmiths day in and day out, delving into the culture and techniques behind Miao silverware. She even joins master silversmiths for a live-stream event, before engaging in discussions with university professors about how traditional craftsmanship can fuel rural revitalization. On top of that, she witnesses the breathtaking sight of "maidens adorned in silver and flowers" at the grand Miao New Year celebrations, visits Xijiang Qianhu Miaozhai — the world’s largest Miao village — and learns to forge a small yet meaningful piece of Miao silver ornament.

programme.title: World Heritage in China: Ancient City of Pingyao
programme.desc: Established in the 14th century, Pingyao retains the typical layout of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China. The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: Tales in Light and Shadow
programme.desc: Beijing shadow puppets bring ancient Chinese tales to life with intricately crafted leather figures. Behind an illuminated screen, these colorful silhouettes dance, enacting epic stories and folklore accompanied by traditional music. Discover this captivating performing art, a cherished part of China's rich cultural tapestry and a mesmerizing visual spectacle.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Fiery Tales of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In this episode, our host takes you to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province, to celebrate the most traditional Torch Festival with the local Yi people. Water nourishes the farmland; fire brings light and warmth. Water and fire are the two essential elements that sustain the life of the Yi people. Puge County is known as the birthplace of the Yi Torch Festival. Our host travels across mountains to the remote heart of Puge County, in search of the origins of the Yi torch, to learn about local daily life, explore the profound Yi culture, and visit a Yi family to share a special “reunion dinner” on the eve of the Torch Festival—just like their own New Year's Eve feast. Together with the locals, we celebrate their most magnificent festival: the Torch Festival.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan’s explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of “opening the gate”, the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou’s rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: Quanzhou Puppet Theater: China’s "Pinocchio Adventure"
programme.desc: In the film, the puppet Pinocchio, carved and created by an old carpenter, comes to life as a real human. Puppets are lifeless by nature—it is the masterful skills of their puppeteers’ fingertips that breathe life into them. What does China’s own "Pinocchio Adventure" look like? This episode takes you into the world of Quanzhou String Puppet Theater. Explore behind-the-scenes stories, from the intricate carving of puppet heads to the art of puppet performance, and witness how the dance of ten fingers and threads weaves a thousand vivid characters to life!

programme.title: Young star on green field
programme.desc: Meet Sun Chenxi, a 12-year-old soccer "star" from Ningbo who first picked up the game at the age of four and is already playing with the confidence of a veteran. Sun says he dreams of turning pro one day and leading China's men's team to the World Cup. Dribbling and passing with skills far more advanced than his age, he has won over audiences far and wide after his father posted clips of Sun flashing his fancy footwork on social media. The soon-to-be-teenager now has millions of followers online. Already recognized as a rising young talent, high hopes are pinned on Sun as he is cheered on by his parents, friends, and throngs of fans online.

programme.title: Escape to Yibin
programme.desc: Yibin is hailed as "The First City along the Yangtze River", home to renowned Yibin Ranmian noodles and Wuliangye liquor. We explored plenty of lesser-known scenic spots: Lizhuang, the cultural hub during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression; vast bamboo groves that embody the hermit culture of China; and the mysterious cliff-hanging coffins. It is precisely these secluded and strategically advantageous lands that enabled local cultures to be well preserved amid turbulent times.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 1
programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. From its Porcelain Tower - one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, to its grand city walls and ancient palaces, join us on a voyage across time to experience the echoes of history in Nanjing's storied bricks.

programme.title: New Year with the Miao
programme.desc: In this episode, it’s Miao New Year, and that means multitudes of merrymaking! Fishing, drinking, bullfighting… Join the host Min-Zhui Lee, among the magnificent mountains of Leishan, where it’s all happening for the ethnic Miao.

programme.title: World Heritages in Handan
programme.desc: Handan, a renowned historical and cultural city in China, boasts abundant cultural and tourism resources, including the Handan Museum and Congtai Park in Congtai District, as well as the Xiangtangshan Grottoes, Guangfu Ancient City, Cizhou Kiln, etc. Handan also has a long-standing connection with the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, a world cultural heritage. As a great project created in ancient China, the Grand Canal has not only exerted a profound impact on cities along the route in terms of transportation, economy and culture, but also served as an important driving force for Handan's development.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: De la misma sangre
programme.desc: Un policia trata de proteger a su hermano, quien trabaja para un poderoso narcotraficante.

programme.title: Que parezca un accidente
programme.desc: Una mujer esta planeando matar a su yerno despues de enterarse de que es infiel a su hija.

programme.title: Lleno de ruido y dolor
programme.desc: En la Patagonia de 1928, un joven inexperto se arrepiente de robar un banco junto con dos bandoleros cuando las cosas no resultan como esperaba.

En el año 2044, una mutacion de la plaga trajo la aniquilacion a tres cuartos de la humanidad. Los que quedan se han organizado en refugios distantes, y afuera, bandas de saqueadores controlan el territorio.

programme.title: La Niña de los Tacones Amarillos
programme.desc: Una chica de 15 años que trabaja en la construcción de un nuevo hotel descubre el efecto que tiene sobre los hombres.

programme.desc: Un joven niño costarricense intenta ayudar a su hermano mayor, quien se ha enfrentado a un peligroso traficante de drogas.
